newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Costa Rica, Portugal win Security Council seats.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica, Portugal win Security Council seats.

text.p: Costa Rica, Japan, Kenya, Portugal and Sweden were elected by the General Assembly Monday to two-year terms on the Security Council, beginning on January 1, 1997.
Japan, Kenya and Sweden were elected after receiving the required two-thirds majority of those voting in the Assembly on the first ballot. Portugal and Costa Rica were elected on the second ballot.

In what had been widely seen as a particularly hotly-contested race, Japan easily beat out India on the first ballot by 142 votes to 40. A two-thirds majority of the 180 delegations voting was required for election on that round.
Kenya, the uncontested candidate for a seat reserved for a member of the African group, received 172 votes.

Sweden, one of three candidates for two seats reserved for members of the West European and Others group, obtained 153 votes on the first ballot. This left Portugal, with 112 votes, and Australia, with 91, to battle it out in the second round. Portugal then obtained 124 votes to only 57 for Australia.

Costa Rica, which obtained 105 votes on the first round, and Bolivia, with 73, both failed to win election on the first round. Bolivia then dropped out, under a pre-election agreement with its rival, and Costa Rica romped home with 167 votes on the second round, although five delegations still cast ballots for Bolivia.
